To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Wearable-based exergames are effective in promoting physical activity in the short term, but the effectiveness decreases over time, and can be reversed by updating the games periodically with novel features and challenges."

(1) users’ motivation and engagement with a gamified exergame decreases over time; (2) periodic updates of the exergame can help reverse the decrease in user engagement; and (3) the effect of the updates on user engagement decreases over time.

1) users' engagement in exergames using activity trackers declines significantly with the passage of time, 2) this decline can be reversed with periodic updates to exergames, and 3) the frequency of updates has a significant effect on users' engagement in wearable-based exergame.

the following questions: (1) How can we increase engagement and retention of users of wearable exergames?
the question: how can we keep users engaged with exergames in the long term?
how to increase the user engagement in exergames, by using the activity trackers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the user engagement and usage of the wearable-based exergame can be maintained for a long duration by periodically pushing out feature updates.
the usage of the game is significantly higher with updates than without updates.
the usage of exergames with activity trackers, even when gamification is employed, sees a consistent decrease over time, and can be reversed with periodic feature updates to the game.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of wearable activity trackers in exergames is a promising way to promote physical activity, but the user engagement needs to be constantly monitored and updated to prevent the user from losing interest.

, while the use of wearable activity trackers to gamify exercise is a good idea, it is necessary that the gamification is done with an understanding of user engagement patterns, and with the use of appropriate game updates.
, in the case of exergames, the user experience is not only about the game, but also about the device and the platform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while exergames can be used to motivate users to exercise, the usage of exergames and activity trackers can decline significantly over time, but can be reversed with periodic updates.
periodic updates to a game, which is designed to be played over a long period of time, can significantly increase the engagement of users.
the use of gamification in wearable exergames should be accompanied by a continuous effort to update and improve them.
